alt: Panorama of Berat with its white Ottoman houses stacked up the hillside above the Osum river.
caption: Berat, the 'city of a thousand windows', on the Osum river. It is the first overnight of the drive, and its Ottoman-era houses climb the slope up to the castle district that is still lived in.

alt: Grey stone houses with slate roofs on the steep slope of Gjirokastër old town.
caption: The stone tower-houses of Gjirokastër, a UNESCO-listed Ottoman town built on a steep ridge. The group sleeps here on day 3 after the Benja hot springs and walks the bazaar streets before the castle.

alt: Excavated stone ruins of the forum at Butrint among trees beside the lagoon.
caption: The forum area at Butrint, an ancient city in a national park on the Vivari channel opposite Corfu. In March it is quiet enough to walk the Greek, Roman and Byzantine layers without crowds.

alt: The small medieval church of Sveti Jovan Kaneo on a cliff above Lake Ohrid.
caption: Sveti Jovan at Kaneo, the cliff-top church above Lake Ohrid. Two nights in Ohrid give a spare day for the old town, Samuel's fortress and the monastery at Sveti Naum, with weather as the deciding factor.

alt: The walled old town of Kotor at the foot of steep mountains on the Bay of Kotor.
caption: Kotor, a Venetian-walled town at the head of a deep, fjord-like bay, with limestone mountains rising behind. In March the old town is walkable without the cruise-ship crowds of summer.

alt: Crno jezero, the Black Lake, ringed by forest below the Durmitor massif.
caption: Crno jezero (Black Lake) below the Durmitor massif near Žabljak. In February or March the lake is usually frozen or ringed by snow, and the circuit is a snowshoe-or-boots walk, not the summer stroll.

alt: The concrete arch bridge of Đurđevića Tara spanning the deep Tara river canyon.
caption: The Đurđevića Tara bridge, a 1940 concrete arch high over the Tara canyon, about 20 minutes' drive from Žabljak. It is the one viewpoint on the Tara that is realistic in winter, as the road is kept open and the canyon is visible from the bridge.

alt: The Ottoman-era Baščaršija bazaar quarter of Sarajevo in winter.
caption: Baščaršija, Sarajevo's Ottoman bazaar quarter, in winter. Coppersmith lanes, coffee houses and the ćevapi grills are all open in February and March, and the smell of charcoal carries on cold days.

alt: The Sarajevo Tunnel Museum building and grounds beside the airport.
caption: The Tunnel of Hope museum at Butmir, built around the house where the 1993 supply tunnel emerged under the airport runway. A short stretch of the 800-metre-plus tunnel can be walked, with a film and a collection of wartime objects.

alt: The Old Bridge and the old town of Mostar over the Neretva river.
caption: Stari Most and the old town of Mostar on the Neretva, rebuilt after the 1990s war. The group spends day 14 here for the bridge, the Ottoman bazaar and the east-west line of the city still marked by war damage.

commonsFile: File:Blagaj Tekke, the spring of the Buna river, Bosnia and Herzegovina 01.jpg
alt: The Blagaj Dervish house built into a cliff at the source of the Buna river.
caption: The Blagaj Tekke, a Sufi dervish house built against a cliff over the source of the Buna river. It is a 15-minute drive from Mostar and one of the clearest examples of Ottoman religious architecture on the trip.

alt: A plate of Bosnian ćevapi with flatbread and onions in Sarajevo.
caption: Ćevapi, small grilled minced-meat sausages served in somun flatbread with raw onion, the everyday Sarajevo lunch. It sits alongside Albanian byrek and Ohrid lake trout as the trip's main regional dishes.
